stories.title: OpenAI and Broadcom Unveil Jalapeño: A Custom LLM Inference Chip
stories.rationale: Custom silicon purpose-built for LLM inference from a top-2 AI lab is a landmark compute event directly aligned with chip and infrastructure interests.
stories.summary: OpenAI and Broadcom jointly introduced Jalapeño, a custom chip designed specifically for large language model inference workloads to improve performance, energy efficiency, and deployment scale. The chip is intended to reduce inference costs and improve throughput across OpenAI's production systems.

stories.title: OpenAI Previews GPT-5.6 Series: Sol, Terra, and Luna with Concrete Pricing Tiers
stories.rationale: Multi-tier flagship model release with concrete cost data (Terra 2× cheaper than GPT-5.5; Luna lowest-cost) and a U.S. government preview constitutes a primary-source major model event.
stories.summary: OpenAI began a limited preview of the GPT-5.6 series comprising Sol (flagship with stronger coding, science, and cybersecurity capabilities), Terra (competitive with GPT-5.5 at 2× lower cost), and Luna (fastest and most affordable tier). The company shared plans with the U.S. government ahead of anticipated general availability in the coming weeks.

stories.title: Samsung Electronics Deploys ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to Employees Worldwide
stories.rationale: Named, large-scale enterprise AI rollout with specific tools deployed to a global workforce is exactly the kind of concrete deployment data the reader values.
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics is rolling out ChatGPT Enterprise and OpenAI's Codex to employees across the company in what OpenAI describes as one of its largest enterprise AI deployments to date. The initiative covers coding assistance and knowledge-worker productivity use cases at global scale.

stories.title: Google DeepMind Introduces Computer Use in Gemini 3.5 Flash
stories.rationale: Agentic computer-use capability in a fast, low-cost model from a top lab is directly relevant to coding agents and SDLC automation interests.
stories.summary: Google DeepMind announced computer use capabilities in Gemini 3.5 Flash, enabling the model to autonomously control computer interfaces and complete desktop and web tasks. The feature extends Gemini's agentic footprint in a model tier optimized for speed and cost efficiency.

stories.title: Asian AI Startups Launch Frontier-Class Models as Anthropic Export Restrictions Drag On
stories.rationale: Geopolitical fragmentation of the frontier model market is structurally important; TechCrunch coverage warrants verification but the trend has significant market implications.
stories.summary: According to TechCrunch, Asian AI startups are releasing models with capabilities comparable to Anthropic's export-restricted models as U.S. controls continue to delay access to Anthropic technology in those markets. The report frames this as accelerating non-U.S. frontier AI development and contributing to geopolitical divergence in model availability.

stories.title: OpenAI Launches Daybreak: AI-Powered Vulnerability Discovery, Patch Automation, and Open-Source Security Support
stories.rationale: AI-driven security tooling for software supply chains (Codex Security, GPT-5.5-Cyber, Patch the Planet) is directly relevant to SDLC automation interests.
stories.summary: OpenAI introduced Daybreak, a security initiative bundling Codex Security for large-scale AI-assisted vulnerability discovery, GPT-5.5-Cyber for cybersecurity tasks, and a 'Patch the Planet' program to help open-source maintainers find and remediate vulnerabilities with AI and expert review. The initiative is positioned as enterprise-scale security automation for organizations of all sizes.

stories.title: Ford AI Automation Initiative 'Backfired Badly,' Report Says
stories.rationale: A named large-enterprise AI deployment failure is a concrete cautionary data point on real-world AI adoption, even though specifics require verification.
stories.summary: The Independent reports that Ford's push to replace human workers with AI-driven automation encountered significant problems, with the effort described as having 'backfired badly.' Specific failure modes are not detailed in available summaries and primary company statements should be sought to corroborate the account.

stories.title: German Court Holds Google Liable for AI Overview Errors; Calls Grow for Broad AI Publisher Liability
stories.rationale: A concrete court ruling establishing AI product liability has direct implications for enterprise AI deployment governance and risk assessment.
stories.summary: A German court ruled that Google is liable for factual errors in its AI Overviews feature, treating AI-generated content as the publisher's legal responsibility rather than a technical disclaimer. Security researcher Bruce Schneier argues this principle should apply broadly: AI agents deployed by companies should be treated in law as those companies' agents, closing any accountability gap.

stories.title: OpenAI Research: AI Agents Enable Longer-Horizon, More Complex Work Tasks Across Professional Roles
stories.rationale: Primary research on agent productivity and task complexity expansion is directly relevant to agentic AI interests, with potential for concrete findings.
stories.summary: OpenAI published research documenting how AI agents are shifting work patterns by enabling longer-horizon and more complex tasks across professional roles, expanding the capability ceiling rather than merely accelerating existing workflows. The paper examines productivity effects as agents take on multi-step, sustained workloads that previously required sustained human coordination.

stories.title: Research: Prompt Injection Reframed as Role Confusion Between Privileged and Attacker-Controlled Text
stories.rationale: Foundational security research with a novel theoretical framework for prompt injection has direct implications for safe agentic system deployment.
stories.summary: MIT researchers Charles Ye, Jasmine Cui, and Dylan Hadfield-Menell propose that prompt injection attacks are best understood as role confusion—models failing to distinguish their own privileged system-level text from attacker-controlled input wrapped in similar formats. The paper suggests that enforcing clearer role boundaries in model architecture and prompting strategies could reduce injection vulnerability.
